# Oracle Sim

> A BattleBots Pro League 2026 prediction model, scraped live via Bright Data, presented as a
> stress test rather than as a working oracle. The central result is a measured negative:
> a small-data model becomes dangerously confident long before it becomes accurate.

Built at the BattleBots Hack Night, London, 28 July 2026. Vanilla JS, no build step, no runtime
API key. All scraped data and the raw page cache are committed, so every number reproduces
offline.

## Headline numbers (reproduce with `node battlebots-sim/tools/eval.mjs`)

- Accuracy 56.5% on 23 fights; record-only baseline 41.3%
- Brier 0.424, where 0.25 is the score for always predicting 50/50
- Calibration failure: the 90-100% confidence bucket is correct 30% of the time
- McNemar exact p = 1.00, with b = 0 and c = 0: model and baseline never once disagreed
- Betting the model over the season: bankroll 1000 -> 246
- The +15.2 point "lift" over baseline is NOT claimed as a result; it is not significant

## Data provenance summary

- battlebots.fandom.com via Bright Data Web Unlocker: 25 pages, 24 bots, 23 fights
- x.com via Bright Data Scraper API dataset gd_lwxkxvnf1cynvib9co: 40 posts, 10 bots mentioned
- youtube.com via Bright Data Scraper API dataset gd_lk9q0ew71spt1mxywf: 470 comments across 15
  Pro League episode videos, 21 of 24 bots mentioned (Tombstone 50, Skorpios 48, HyperShock 20)
- reddit.com via Bright Data Scraper API dataset gd_lvz8ah06191smkebj4: 497 r/battlebots posts,
  16 of 24 bots discussed (HUGE 18 posts / 9,649 upvotes, Tombstone 16)
- gamma-api.polymarket.com via Web Unlocker: no BattleBots market exists
- Web Unlocker refuses all three social platforms (x.com, reddit.com, youtube.com) on robots.txt
  grounds. All three were reached through their dedicated Scraper API datasets instead. Every
  refusal was a routing problem, not a wall.

## Notable engineering results

- The logistic fit diverged to NaN at l2 >= 6 while still reporting 69.6% accuracy, making the
  broken model the best-looking cell in the hyperparameter sweep. Cause: gradient descent with
  weight decay is stable only while lr*l2 < 2. Fixed by scaling the step.
- Mining every competitor's full career results table off the already-cached pages produced 559
  raw results, deduped to 455 unique fights. Training on 113 fights instead of 23 improved Brier
  from 0.424 to 0.299 but dropped accuracy to 46%, below chance. The problem was data relevance,
  not data volume.
- Fetch route is recorded per page at fetch time, so a cache-served run cannot inherit a Bright
  Data provenance it only partly has.
- Scraper API validation errors are the contract: each rejection names the field or discovery
  mode it will not accept, so the input narrows until accepted. Generalising one early refusal
  into "this platform is unavailable" nearly cost the project its three richest sources.

## Verification commands

- `node battlebots-sim/tools/eval.mjs` - model, calibration, McNemar, learned weights
- `node battlebots-sim/tools/bet.mjs` - season P&L; add `--l2 3` for the regularised comparison
- `node battlebots-sim/tools/sweep.mjs` - hyperparameter grid
- `node battlebots-sim/scrape/test_parsers.mjs` - parser and validator tests
- `node battlebots-sim/scrape/career.mjs` - re-derive the 455 career fights from cached pages
- `node battlebots-sim/tools/qa.cjs` - headless browser test, requires a static server on 8099
